hanke-hormuz-9m-claim-vs-tracked-1_74m:
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the oil leaving the Strait of Hormuz is running at close to 9 million barrels a day on a seven-day average.
The firms that count the same strait with satellites and ship signals report numbers far below that.

@@REF@@Wright claims Persian Gulf oil trade is back at pre-Iran-war levels (Washington Examiner, 2026-08-12)|https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/energy-and-environment/4683048/chris-wright-claims-persian-gulf-oil-trade-pre-iran-war-levels/|https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-collage-cpi5u167u-1782322561169-e1782324080180.jpg?1786457655&resize=1200,683

The Strait of Hormuz is the only sea exit from the Persian Gulf.
How much oil moves through it sets the floor under the world oil price.

## What the strait carried before

@@BAR@@Normal traffic (first half of 2025)|20.9 million barrels a day|2090|Energy Secretary's seven-day average|9 million barrels a day|900|Kpler figure cited by Hanke (week of August 3)|1.74 million barrels a day|174@@All three numbers describe the same strait. Which one you pick changes the amount of oil the world is currently losing by more than tenfold.@@US Energy Information Administration, World Oil Transit Chokepoints (updated 2026-03-03) · Secretary Wright's post (2026-08-11) · Kpler figure cited by Hanke (2026-08-15) · retrieved 2026-08-16

The Energy Information Administration put flows through the strait at 20.9 million barrels a day in the first half of 2025.
That is one quarter of all crude oil traded by sea passing through a single narrow channel.

## The split is over what gets counted

@@CMP@@The Secretary's reading|Count everything leaving the Gulf. Add the 5 to 7 million barrels a day moving through new bypass pipelines to what crosses the strait and the total is not far from pre-war levels.|The ship-trackers' reading|Count only the vessels that actually transit. Oil in a pipeline never crossed the strait, and a ship with its position signal switched off cannot be counted at all.

Both sides are looking at the same water and drawing the boundary of the count in different places.

The interesting part is that the critics do not agree with each other either.
Commodity analyst Rory Johnston puts the seven-day average at about 7 million barrels a day and calls 9 million a stretch; Gregory Brew of Eurasia Group puts it near 5 million.
The Kpler figure Hanke cites is another three times smaller than that.

@@REF@@Tanker data challenges US claim of Gulf oil flow recovery (AGBI, 2026-08-12)|https://www.agbi.com/analysis/oil-and-gas/2026/08/tanker-data-challenges-us-claim-of-gulf-oil-flow-recovery/|https://www.agbi.com/tachyon/sites/4/2026/08/2026-07-14T120508Z_2066010026_MT1SIPA000CY121T_RTRMADP_3_SIPA-USA-scaled.jpg

Counting hulls instead of barrels sharpens the picture.
Kpler's ten-day average came to 11 transits a day, against more than 20 a day before the crisis.

## What the bypass pipelines can actually carry

The largest single line in the Secretary's arithmetic is the oil that skips the strait entirely.
Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline can nominally push 7 million barrels a day across the country.

The Red Sea terminal at Yanbu where that oil is loaded, however, can only handle 4.5 to 5 million barrels a day.
A wide pipe into a narrow port exports at the rate of the port.

The Emirati line to Fujairah currently runs 1.8 million barrels a day, and the work to roughly double it is about half finished, targeted at 2027.
That is why Johnston measures actual pipeline throughput at around 4 million barrels a day.

@@REF@@Gulf states race to build Hormuz bypass infrastructure (Kpler, 2026-07-10)|https://www.kpler.com/blog/new-pipelines-bypassing-the-strait-of-hormuz-could-come-online-in-1-2-years|https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65059ad784ac02253c62356c/6a58b9d872b4d22f22e4a70d_thumbnail_Strait_of_Hormuz_77077bdae8.jpg

## August 14, and two Emirati tankers

Hanke wrote that 56 tankers crossed the strait on August 14 last year and 4 crossed on the same date this year.
That single day's count cannot be verified from public data, but what happened that day can.

@@REF@@UAE accuses Iran of attacks on two state oil company vessels in the Strait of Hormuz (Al Jazeera, 2026-08-14)|https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/14/uae-accuses-iran-of-attacks-on-two-adnoc-vessels-in-strait-of-hormuz|https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/getty_6a7e5499b4-1786664089.jpg?resize=1920%2C1440

The United Arab Emirates said two tankers belonging to its state oil company were attacked in the strait that day.
The thin traffic is not a quirk of the statistics. It is attached to what happened on the water.

The price of passage tells the same story.
War risk premiums that ran at a quarter of one percent of hull value before the conflict now run between 3% and 10%.
For a $200 million tanker that is millions of dollars in premium for a single voyage, which means owners are staying away not because the channel is blocked but because the arithmetic no longer works.

So the argument is less about who is right than about which number you plan the next quarter around.
If Kpler's weekly average climbs above 9 million barrels a day before the end of the fourth quarter, the Secretary's account is supported; if it stays under that line through the quarter, the ship data was the better guide.
kobeissi-jolts-initiation-rate-one-in-fo:
America's job-openings figure is built from the roughly one in four businesses that agree to answer, the source says.
Before the pandemic, the source says, that share ran between half and seven in ten.

@@REF@@Fewer people, businesses are responding to government requests for data (Marketplace, 2025-08-13)|https://www.marketplace.org/story/2025/08/13/what-happens-when-government-survey-participation-falls|https://img.apmcdn.org/4fccee7917ce412e8b1ffa7e2faca7ab401deb9b/widescreen/cd44ec-20250813-executive-woman-hand-filling-out-form-2000.jpg

Reporting on the same trend uses a slightly different yardstick.
The share of businesses taking part in government surveys fell from 75% in 2015 to 35% in April 2025.

@@BAR@@Business participation, 2015|75%|75|April 2025|35%|35@@That is how much of the answering side disappeared in ten years. The surveys did not get harder to fill in. The firms stopped filling them in.@@Marketplace, 2025-08-13, citing BLS figures. Retrieved 2026-08-16.

## A survey that waits 45 days for an answer

The Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey draws a sample of 21,000 establishments and collects answers over about 45 days.
Nobody is legally required to reply. Only the firms that want to reply do.

The release date arrives before the answers do.
So the BLS publishes a number from whatever has come in, then corrects it the following month as the late answers land.
The June openings figure came out on August 4, and on the same day May was cut by 57,000.

@@CHK@@June job openings|7.4 million|June unemployed|7.1 million|Openings per unemployed worker|1.0@@A labor market sitting at neither tight nor slack. The call turns on the first decimal place, and the sample that produces that decimal is thinning out.@@US Bureau of Labor Statistics, released 2026-08-04 for June, TED post 2026-08-07. Retrieved 2026-08-16.

One opening for every unemployed worker.
This is one of the ratios the Federal Reserve is known to reach for when it asks whether the labor market is running hot, and job openings are the numerator.
Shake the numerator and you shake the judgment.

## The budget behind the missing replies

The BLS budget was $636 million in fiscal 2025.
The fiscal 2026 request came in at $580 million, down 11.8%, and the same document carries a plan to cut staff by 17%.
When the money went, the collecting went first.
Consumer price collection stopped in Lincoln, Nebraska and Provo, Utah in April 2025, and in Buffalo, New York in May.
Three hundred and fifty detailed producer price indexes were dropped, and two federal advisory committees that watched over economic statistics were closed in March 2025.

@@REF@@A Long-Overdue Reckoning For The Bureau Of Labor Statistics (Forbes, 2025-08-13)|https://www.forbes.com/sites/georgecalhoun/2025/08/13/a-long-overdue-reckoning-for-the-bureau-of-labor-statistics/|https://imageio.forbes.com/specials-images/imageserve/689cc825723be15e7caa6bc4/0x0.jpg?format=jpg&height=900&width=1600&fit=bounds

That piece reads the problem not as a mistake by the agency but as a bill that had been deferred for years.
What went missing is not the numbers. It is the people and the legwork that make the numbers.

## June, recalculated on September 1

None of this is hidden.
Since March 13, 2026 the BLS has been publishing the response-rate series for the job openings survey in its public database.
Few people read it.

July job openings arrive on September 1, and June gets corrected the same day.
If the correction is smaller than 57,000, the late answers cannot move the first print much.
If it is bigger, then a market that has been reading each first print at face value has been trading a different number every month.
Either way, the thing worth watching is not how high job openings are. It is how far the figure travels afterwards.

About half of the copper still sitting in London Metal Exchange warehouses has already been claimed for withdrawal.
Stockpiles have fallen for 42 straight trading days,
and over that stretch anyone who needs metal today has ended up paying far more than someone willing to wait a month.

@@REF@@Copper price holds near record as London warehouse bidding war looms (Mining.com, 2026-08-14)|https://www.mining.com/copper-price-holds-near-record-as-london-warehouse-bidding-war-looms/|https://www.mining.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/AdobeStock_588953684-e1770662316198.jpeg

## Why the date matters more than the price

In commodity markets the later delivery is usually the dearer one.
Storage and financing costs get added on top.

When that order flips and the immediate delivery becomes the expensive one, the market is in backwardation.
Put simply, there is not enough metal in the warehouse, so whoever cannot wait pays a premium to jump the queue.
The binding question stops being what copper costs and becomes when you can actually take hold of it.

@@CHK@@LME copper stocks|204,975 tonnes|Consecutive days of decline|42|Metal booked for withdrawal|about half of what is left|Cash to three month price gap|$434 a tonne|August to September price gap|$370 a tonne|LME cash price|about $14,500 a tonne@@The falling stockpile matters less than the fact that half of what remains already has an owner waiting. A front position trading hundreds of dollars a tonne above the one behind it says a great many buyers cannot afford to be without metal right now.@@Figures as reported by Mining.com, 2026-08-14, accessed 2026-08-15

## The copper did not disappear, it moved

@@FLOW@@Tariff signalled|The market comes to expect a US duty on refined copper|Metal relocates|Producers and traders ship copper into US warehouses before any duty lands|London stocks drain|What is left in London shrinks while withdrawal requests pile up|Front premium|Buyers who need metal now pay far above those content to wait a month@@The copper was not consumed, it crossed the Atlantic. That is why this squeeze will not be undone by mines digging faster, and why it turns first on how the tariff is written.

There is one thing the Kobeissi Letter did not mention.

@@REF@@Indonesia smelter failure extends copper record rally as global stockpiles near crisis (TechTimes, 2026-08-11)|https://www.techtimes.com/articles/323984/20260811/indonesia-smelter-failure-extends-copper-record-rally-global-stockpiles-near-crisis.htm|https://d.techtimes.com/en/full/472271/indonesia-smelter-failure-extends-copper-record-rally-as-global-stockpiles-near-crisis.jpg

On August 8 a boiler water leak shut the Gresik smelter in East Java, Indonesia, for checks and repairs.
The plant makes about 342,000 tonnes of copper cathode a year and takes its ore solely from Grasberg, the second largest copper mine in the world.
It is owned jointly by Freeport Indonesia and Japan's Mitsubishi Materials.

If the pre-tariff shipments pulled existing copper to one side of the ocean, the outage cut the amount coming out of the ground into metal for several weeks.
The original post covers the first force. The second arrived at the same moment and pushed the same way.

## The numbers on the table are 15 percent in 2027 and 30 percent in 2028

What the market is really pricing is not copper supply and demand but a decision in Washington.
A phased duty is being discussed, with talk of 15 percent from 2027 rising to 30 percent from 2028.

If those numbers are confirmed, the copper already moved into the United States turns out to have been bought before the price of entry went up, and emptying the London sheds looks like a gain rather than a loss.
A lower or delayed duty flips it.
The metal parked in US warehouses gains a reason to come back out, and today's premium on immediate delivery goes away quickly.

So the thing to watch here is not the daily copper price but how fast the booked metal actually leaves the warehouses, and when the tariff decision lands.
Which of those two moves first will settle whether today's price was justified.
elerian-blanchard-france-multiple-equili:
The expectation that the European Central Bank will buy your government bonds comes with conditions that are written down.
The first one is not being subject to an excessive deficit procedure, or, if subject to one, not being assessed as having failed to take effective action in response to a Council recommendation.
France has been subject to that procedure since July 2024.

@@REF@@The Transmission Protection Instrument (European Central Bank press release, 2022-07-21)|https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2022/html/ecb.pr220721~973e6e7273.en.html|https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/shared/img/socialmedia/social-default.jpg?0ef1632c35edede913681bb76af694a4

The reason this comes up now is a post Olivier Blanchard wrote on August 15 about France's public finances, which Mohamed El-Erian passed along with the note that the framework fits some other economies too.

## What the phrase multiple equilibria points at

Multiple equilibria describes a situation in which the same conditions can produce two different outcomes.
If investors believe the debt is safe, rates stay low and it can indeed be serviced; if they believe it is unsafe, rates rise and servicing really does become hard.
Belief produces the outcome.

It works like a run on a bank.
If everyone thinks the money is there, it is; if everyone goes to withdraw at once, it genuinely is not.

@@FLOW@@Safe zone|Debt is clearly serviceable and the central bank has nothing to do|Danger zone|A good outcome and a bad one sit side by side, and the bad one is avoided if the central bank buys when private investors sell|Default zone|Debt is clearly not serviceable, fiscal policy has to be adjusted first, and this is not the central bank's job@@Each zone calls for a different response, so not knowing which one you are standing in means not being able to pick the response.

This is where Blanchard puts his finger.
When investors demand a higher risk premium, the central bank does not know for sure whether this is the danger zone, where it should step in, or already the default zone, where absent an adjustment programme it should not.
So it leans toward asking for the programme first, and counting on it to remove the bad equilibrium on its own, he wrote, is unwise.

## Which zone France is standing in

@@BAR@@France|117.6%|117.6|Italy|138.9%|138.9|Euro area average|88.9%|88.9|Germany|64.4%|64.4@@Countries sharing one currency sit this far apart. That is why no single number draws the line where the danger zone begins.@@Retrieved 2026-08-15 · Eurostat government debt release (2026-07-21) · Q1 2026

@@REF@@Government debt in the euro area, first quarter of 2026 (Eurostat, 2026-07-21)|https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-euro-indicators/w/2-21072026-ap|https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/2995521/18500178/New Africa_AdobeStock_521389990_RV.jpg/6d6a3c42-5eb3-03d6-555d-a19fafaa1117

The rating agencies have moved one way.
Moody's cut in December 2024, Fitch followed in September 2025 and S&P in October 2025.
France now carries A+ at S&P and Fitch, and one notch above that at Moody's, which is the only one attaching a negative outlook.
That is not the rating of a country facing default, and it is not a rating that tells you the country is in the safe zone either.
It is closest to the middle of Blanchard's three zones, and the middle is precisely the one where the answer is not settled.

## The four lines written on July 21, 2022

When the ECB created a purchase tool called the Transmission Protection Instrument on July 21, 2022, it published four eligibility criteria alongside it.
Compliance with the EU fiscal framework, the absence of severe macroeconomic imbalances, debt sustainability, and sound and sustainable macroeconomic policies.

The first criterion reads as not being subject to an excessive deficit procedure, or not being assessed as having failed to take effective action in response to an EU Council recommendation.
France entered that procedure on July 26, 2024, and on January 21, 2025 the Council adopted a recommendation to correct the deficit by 2029.
The European Commission's compliance report of June 3, 2026 still lists France among the countries with an open procedure.

The conjunction in that sentence carries weight.
Being subject to the procedure does not by itself remove eligibility; eligibility survives if the country is assessed as taking effective action.
France's standing therefore rests with the Commission's assessment rather than with the ECB.
Where Blanchard expects the central bank to ask for an adjustment programme first, he is restating something already set down as a condition.

No instance of the instrument actually being activated could be found.
That it has stood unused for four years is itself part of what has held markets in place.

How much of an expectation that the central bank will buy belongs in the price of the bonds is what splits here.
Fitch reviews France again on August 28.
If the rating holds, the ground stays where it is; one notch lower and the market starts reading the conditions instead.

Japan protested through diplomatic channels on July 31 after confirming that China had started installing another structure in the East China Sea.
The boundary between the two countries is still undelimited there, and by the count Japanese wires have kept, this is structure number twenty-four.

@@REF@@New movement by China concerning unilateral development of natural resources in the East China Sea (Japan MOFA, 2026-07-31)|https://www.mofa.go.jp/press/release/pressite_000001_02559.html

The ministry's own release does not say which number it is.
The count came from Jiji Press the same day; a year earlier Nikkei put the running total at twenty-one.

@@CHK@@Chinese structures confirmed by Japan (August 2025)|21|Same count (July 31, 2026)|24@@Three more in a year. The seabed is being occupied faster than the treaty clock runs.@@Retrieved 2026-08-15 · Japan MOFA release (2026-07-31) · Jiji Press and Nikkei counts

The water these structures stand in runs right up against the block Korea calls Block 7.

## What comes due on June 22, 2028

Block 7 sits on a sedimentary basin that begins south of Jeju Island.
It lies closer to Japan by distance, but the continental shelf under it runs back toward Korea, and in 1974 the two countries agreed to develop it together and split anything they found down the middle.
The agreement entered into force on June 22, 1978, for a term of fifty years.

@@REF@@Future of Korea-Japan joint development zone in doubt (Korea JoongAng Daily, 2024-02-14)|https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/korea/future-of-korea-japan-joint-development-zone-in-doubt/11509987|https://image.koreajoongangdaily.com/11510171.jpg?imageId=11510171&panox=0&panoy=0&panow=0&panoh=0&width=1200&height=683

Either side can end it with three years' notice, and the first day such notice could be given was June 22, 2025.
Japan did not give it that day, according to Yomiuri.

## Reading again the judgment that told Japan to wait

The original post locates Japan's patience in case law.
Natural prolongation, under which the country the shelf runs back to holds the rights, was the dominant doctrine into the 1970s, and the account has the International Court of Justice overturning that in the 1985 Libya-Malta case by ruling for a median line.

Open the judgment and the step does not land there.
The Court declined Malta's argument that equidistance had to be the mandatory starting point, and wrote that natural prolongation and distance are complementary rather than exclusive.
The drift is real: within 200 nautical miles, geological prolongation carries less legal weight than it once did.
What is not in that judgment is a sentence settling the question on a median line.
What kept Japan waiting is a probability leaning one way, not a decided rule.

There is a second place the original does not go.
China and Japan already agreed, in 2008, to develop this same stretch of sea jointly.

@@REF@@Delving deeper: China tests new waters in East China Sea oil and gas (CSIS Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative)|https://amti.csis.org/delving-deeper-china-tests-new-waters-in-east-china-sea-oil-and-gas/|https://amti.csis.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/North-ECS-jack-up-April-5-2026-banner.jpg

That agreement has gone eighteen years without being operationalised, and in the meantime China put its platforms up on the west side of the median line.
Signing something and then running out the clock has already produced one result in this water.

## The path by which Block 7 becomes disputed water

@@FLOW@@June 22, 2028|The Korea-Japan joint development agreement lapses after fifty years|Undelimited water|Neither side is left with settled ground to work it alone|One more party|China gains a place to argue, on natural prolongation, that it holds a share too@@What Japan may gain by waiting is not an exclusive licence but a sea with one more country in the arithmetic.

Korea cannot simply climb onto China's natural prolongation argument either.
China has a broad shelf, and conceding that logic unsettles the Yellow Sea, which the two countries divided on a median line.

The day for giving notice has passed, and less than two years are left.
If Japan moves toward splitting the shares with Korea again, this stays a problem between two countries.
If June 22, 2028 arrives with no notice given, the seabed gets settled before the law does.
The structures keep going up while that runs.

German carmakers and their suppliers shed 42,300 jobs in a single year.
Employment stood at 691,500 at the end of June, the lowest level since 2005.
That is a 5.8% drop.

@@REF@@German car industry sheds jobs at a record pace (dpa, 2026-08-14)|https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/german-car-industry-sheds-jobs-074838681.html|https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/307041C11A078CF9D4200384F95315076DC49968EEC02831DC90EEEBFB6CF15B/subgraphmysterio/resizefit_w960;quality_80;format_webp/https:%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fdpa_international_526%2F4fabc4c6b956bda41f1e7ebb5de89027.jpg

The person who put that number back into circulation is Steve Hanke, a monetary economist.
In the same post he named a single cause.
Cheap Russian gas was cut off, and Germany is at war with Russia, and this is turning the country into an industrial wasteland.

Naming a cause is the kind of claim you can check.
If the price of gas is the culprit, the industries that burn the most gas should be the ones falling apart.

## The industries that burn the most gas

In German manufacturing, the biggest gas consumer is chemicals and pharmaceuticals.
Gas heats their plants, and it is also the raw material that becomes plastics and fertiliser.
Car plants, by comparison, lean on electricity more than on gas.

The accounting firm EY counted German industrial employment for the whole of 2025.
The sector lost 124,000 jobs, and about 50,000 of them were in cars.
Chemicals and pharmaceuticals lost about 2,000.

@@CHK@@Auto jobs lost in 2025|about 50,000|Chemical and pharma jobs lost in 2025|about 2,000|Auto employment, end of June 2026|691,500@@If gas were the cause, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, the heaviest gas users in the country, should have been hit hardest. The industry that actually shrank was cars. The cause Hanke names does not explain that gap.@@Retrieved 2026-08-15 · EY analysis of German industrial employment (dpa, 2026-02-17) · German Federal Statistical Office, H1 2026 count (dpa, 2026-08-14)

@@REF@@Analysis: German industry cut 124,000 jobs in 2025 (dpa, 2026-02-17)|https://finance.yahoo.com/news/analysis-german-industry-cut-124-105835807.html|https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/99BE5755A6A2D4DBA08FD9044108A99B897643DE87A9BE86008D6D2696C1F28C/subgraphmysterio/resizefit_w960;quality_80;format_webp/https:%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fdpa_international_526%2F2b0b454c0963d00d0a9fe93b36e062e9

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Gas_stove_blue_flames.jpg/500px-Gas_stove_blue_flames.jpg|The suspect Hanke names. The cheap Russian gas Germany used to import has been off since 2022.|Marina Burity · CC BY-SA 2.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gas_stove_blue_flames.jpg

In the same study EY listed its own reasons.
German carmakers are moving production abroad, and industrial revenue has fallen almost 5% since 2023.
Energy prices do not appear on that list as a standalone item.

## The segment that added people

Break the statistical office's count into segments and the direction is not uniform.
Parts and accessories makers were down 7.6%, and vehicle manufacturers were down 6.1%.
Bodywork and trailer makers, though, were up 10%, to 42,800.

All three pay the same gas price and the same electricity bill in the same country.
Explain everything with energy and the third segment is left over.

Put simply, this looks less like the whole plant losing power and more like specific lines losing orders.
Bodywork and trailers ride commercial and specialty vehicle demand, while parts suppliers take the full force of production moving abroad and of Chinese competitors.
When two groups pay the same fuel bill and one shrinks while the other grows, what separated them is the order book, not the meter.

## Between 42,300 and 47,000

Hanke's 42,400 differs from the statistical office count by 100. That looks like rounding.
The German automotive industry association published a different survey in February.
It put 2025 employment in the sector at 726,000 and said the year had cost 47,000 jobs.
The scope and the timing differ, so the numbers differ. Which one you quote moves the decline by nearly 5,000 people.

What is at stake is when to look at European auto suppliers again.
If energy costs are the cause, employment returns as gas prices come down.
If the cause is relocation and competition, the decline continues regardless of gas.
If the statistical office's next half-year count, due in August 2027, falls below this year's level again, the cause sits outside energy.

The Strategic Petroleum Reserve is crude stored in 61 salt caverns at four sites on the Gulf Coast.

@@REF@@US strategic oil stockpile nears four-decade low as Iran war drags on (Al-Monitor, 2026-06-11)|https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/06/us-strategic-oil-stockpile-nears-four-decade-low-iran-war-drags|https://www.al-monitor.com/sites/default/files/styles/social_media_share/public/2026-06/GettyImages-2280782890.jpg

That report noted the reserve draining steadily as the war stretched on.
In the two months since, it has fallen further and set a fresh four-decade low.

On August 14 West Texas Intermediate settled at $82.40 a barrel and Brent at $88.52.
Gasoline averaged $4.07 a gallon nationally on August 15.
Barrels went into the market from the reserve, and prices are still here.

## Lent out rather than bought back

Here is the piece the original post leaves out.
There are two ways for the government to put crude back in the caverns.
One is a purchase, paid for out of budget. The other is an exchange, where refiners take barrels now and return barrels later.

@@TIME@@January 7, 1983|294.8 million barrels, back when the reserve was still being built up|January 2010|726.6 million barrels, the all-time peak|November 12, 2025|The Energy Department awards contracts to buy back 1 million barrels|June 10, 2026|Fifth solicitation under the 172-million-barrel release, repaid in barrels rather than cash@@It took 27 years to fill. The last confirmed cash purchase was in November 2025, for 1 million barrels.
Set against the capacity of the caverns, that is a corner of one room.

An exchange is a different animal.
The solicitation posted on June 10 covered 40 million barrels, with refiners taking crude now and returning crude later.
In earlier exchanges, borrowers repaid roughly 26% more than they took.

From the lender's side, it is a way to refill without spending a dollar of budget.
From the borrower's side, it is a bet that expensive oil today will be cheaper oil on the day the barrels have to go back.
Which means refilling the reserve now rides on the future oil price rather than on an appropriation.

## The 125 days the Energy Department cited

The mechanical numbers are simple.
Even after a presidential order it takes 13 days for the crude to reach the market, and no more than 4.4 million barrels a day can be pulled out however urgent it gets.
Members of the International Energy Agency are required to hold reserves equal to 90 days of net imports.
The Energy Department said that at 411 million barrels, where the reserve stood at the end of 2025, the SPR alone covered 125 days.
How many days it covers at today's level is not something published data shows.

The split is whether the barrels that went out on exchange come back as barrels.
If they do, the United States refills the caverns without spending tax money and gets its instrument back before the next supply shock.
If they do not, or if oil spikes again first, the country meets that moment with nothing left to sell into the market.
The question then is not what the price is. It is whether the government still has anything to put against it.

## What making a substrate out of glass means

A semiconductor die does not attach to a motherboard bare.
A thin plate goes in between to carry signals and power across, and today that plate is mostly built from plastic based material.

Switch that plate to glass and it gets thinner while using power more efficiently.
It also warps less under heat, which suits AI accelerators that spread several dies across a wide area.
The TrendForce piece above puts the gain at 25 percent less thickness and more than 30 percent better power efficiency.
The reason it gives for moving is cost. CoWoS, the method used today to tie dies together across a wide area, now runs at a per-unit price on a par with a 7nm class wafer.

## The step that is stuck is not the making

@@FLOW@@Glass blank|A flat panel much like display glass arrives|Drilling|Fine holes linking top to bottom are cut with a laser|Wiring and mounting|Metal fills the holes and circuitry is drawn on|Customer reliability testing|The customer applies heat and stress to see whether it cracks@@Of the four steps, the one that binds is the last. The maker can be ready and the date still moves, because the buyer has to sign off.

When Samsung Electro-Mechanics revised its start to 2028 at the late July second quarter briefing, the reason it gave was customer reliability testing of its prototypes.
Two companies are stuck at the same step.

Glass is hard, and hard things break.

Run heat up and down a panel drilled through with fine holes and cracks can start around those holes.
That is exactly what the customer is testing for.
A verdict arrives only after hundreds of cycles of mounting a die and taking the temperature up and back down.
The plant sits built and waiting through all of it.
That is why the schedule does not move at the maker's pace.

The rule that has the Fed target an average of 2% in order to make up for past low inflation does not exist right now.
The Fed deleted that sentence from its statement on August 22, 2025.

On August 14 Peter Schiff took the rule to be alive and worked out a sum from it.
Inflation has averaged 4% over the past 65 months, so bringing the average back to 2% would take 65 months at 0%.

@@TIME@@2020-08-27|The Fed introduced average inflation targeting at Jackson Hole|2025-08-22|Powell said the Fed had returned to flexible inflation targeting and eliminated the makeup strategy|2026-01-27|The FOMC reaffirmed a statement identical to the August 2025 version|2026-08-14|Schiff published the 65-month sum, resting it on the average 2% target@@The rule the sum rests on left the statement about a year before the sum was written.@@Retrieved 2026-08-15 · Federal Reserve, Powell speech (2025-08-22) · Federal Reserve, FOMC press release (2026-01-27)

## What making up was supposed to mean

Average inflation targeting, adopted in August 2020, was a promise to read the target over a stretch of time rather than at a moment.
If inflation ran below the target for a while, it would be allowed to run above it for a while afterwards so that the average came out right.

@@REF@@What do changes in the Fed's longer-run goals and monetary strategy statement mean? (Brookings, 2020-09-02)|https://www.brookings.edu/articles/what-do-changes-in-the-feds-longer-run-goals-and-monetary-strategy-statement-mean/|https://www.brookings.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/shutterstock_117869614.jpg?quality=50&w=500

Brookings, writing when the framework was new, described a promise with no period attached to it.
Inflation undershooting "for a time" would be answered by overshooting "for some time", and how many months went into the average was left open.
Powell himself called it a flexible form of average inflation targeting.
Because the averaging window was never pinned down, the stretch to be repaid does not fall out of the rule on its own.

## What the Fed said on the day the sentence went

On August 22, 2025, presenting the results of the framework review, Powell said the Fed had returned to flexible inflation targeting and eliminated the makeup strategy.
In the same remarks he said there had been nothing intentional or moderate about the inflation that arrived.

@@REF@@Speech by Chair Powell on the economic outlook and framework review (Federal Reserve Board, 2025-08-22)|https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/powell20250822a.htm|https://www.federalreserve.gov/images/social-media/social-default-image-opengraph.jpg

What went was not a phrase but the ground the sum stands on.
With a makeup clause, past inflation stays on the books as a debt to be repaid.
Without one, 2% from here is enough.
Then on January 27, 2026, at its annual organisational meeting, the FOMC reaffirmed a statement identical to the August 2025 version.
It has stayed deleted for close to a year.

## The arithmetic that survives January 27, 2026

The quarrel is not with the stretch Schiff measured or the average he found.
It is with where those values get entered.

Under the rule as it stands, five years of past inflation is a record rather than a balance owed.
So the sum reads better as a note on what the Fed has decided not to do than as a forecast of what it will do.
Had the makeup clause survived, today's price level would be a reason to hold rates high for years; with it deleted, that reason no longer comes out of the statement.
Whether the Fed turns back toward repaying the past is decided at the next framework review.

@@REF@@Fact sheet: imposing tariffs on drones and their parts and components (The White House, 2026-08-13)|https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2026/08/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-bolsters-national-security-and-strengthens-u-s-supply-chains-by-imposing-tariffs-on-drones-and-their-parts-and-components/|https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/WH47-Social-Share-Card.jpg

The rate comes with a condition. The White House fact sheet says substantially all of the hardware, the software and the technology has to originate in that country or in the United States.
A drone does not fly on its airframe alone. Flight control software, maps and communication modules come with it.
So an aircraft assembled in Korea or Japan still misses the lower bracket if the software inside it fails the origin test.

## American makers pass through the same gate

The original post read the move as good news for US drone component suppliers and aircraft makers.
The direction is right, but one bracket is missing from that reading.
The 25% rate covers a broad set of components, and American manufacturers import a great many of them.
The proclamation gives 180 days to non-sensitive components and to products carrying Department of War or FCC exemptions.
That builds a six-month gap between the moment costs rise and the moment domestic production is meant to stand up.
The same proclamation directs the commerce secretary to set up an onshoring incentive programme, which reads as a device for filling that gap.

## What splits after September 3

What splits here is whether this tariff raises American drone revenue or American drone costs.
If US airframes fill the space that the top tariff clears of imported finished drones, revenue moves first.
If procurement costs rise by the tariff before that, margin moves first.
If gross margins at US drone makers rise from the prior quarter in the first results after September 3, it is the former; if they fall, it is the latter.

What that line would print is the chip that sits at the very bottom of an HBM stack.

@@REF@@Samsung may repurpose an R&D line for foundry, targeting 2nm HBM base dies for future NVIDIA demand (TrendForce, 2026-08-14)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/08/14/news-samsung-may-repurpose-rd-line-for-foundry-targeting-2nm-hbm-base-dies-for-future-nvidia-demand/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/02160941/Samsung-HBM4-624x468.png

## The chip at the bottom of HBM

HBM is memory built by stacking eight to twelve DRAM dies vertically.
At the very bottom sits one more die that is not DRAM.
It marshals the signals the stacked DRAM sends and receives and pushes them out of the package. It is called the base die.

A base die is logic, not memory.
So it is made on a foundry process rather than in a DRAM plant.
Until now a 4nm-class process was enough, but as stacks got taller and speeds higher, heat became the problem.
Doing the same work on less power calls for a finer process, and the answer being floated is 2nm.

## Where the wafers travel

The arrangement described in the report is a "send fab".
Rather than building a product end to end, such a line takes in wafers from other production lines, runs one specific stretch of the process, and sends them back.

@@FLOW@@Production line|Wafers come off Samsung's foundry production lines|NRD-K Line 2|The handed-over wafers get their base die patterned on a 2nm process|HBM stacking|Eight to twelve DRAM dies are stacked on top and bound into one package|Customer|It ships to AI accelerator makers such as NVIDIA@@Once the base die moves to 2nm, what sets HBM's speed is the foundry process, not the DRAM process.

This is where the news actually bites.
The memory contest is shifting from a race to shrink DRAM into a race for a slot on the newest foundry node.
2nm is the node where smartphone application processors and AI chips are already queueing. Memory now wants to join that queue.

@@TIME@@2026-06-02|Samsung showed HBM5 for the first time at Computex|2026-08-14|Korean media reported the review of turning NRD-K Line 2 into a foundry send fab|>2028|Expected start of HBM5 mass production|>H2 2028|Target for bringing the NRD-K complex online@@If the review is real, Samsung is claiming the slot roughly two years before HBM5 starts selling.@@Retrieved 2026-08-15 · TrendForce (2026-08-14) · TrendForce (2026-06-02)

@@REF@@Samsung unveils HBM5 for the first time at Computex, production reportedly seen around 2028 (TrendForce, 2026-06-02)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/06/02/news-samsung-unveils-hbm5-model-for-the-first-time-at-computex-production-reportedly-seen-around-2028/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/02141324/Samsung-HBM5-model-624x617.png

Earlier reporting says HBM5 is expected to run more than 50% faster than HBM4E.
Samsung has said it will spend 20 trillion won building three NRD-K lines by 2030.
One of those three would be changing jobs.

## What one NRD-K line costs

A research line is where the next generation gets tested.
Turn it over to production and the orders in front of you get filled, but the test bench for the generation after that loses a slot.
This is still at the review stage, and the company has announced nothing.

What splits here is whether Samsung fights the HBM war as a memory company or as a company that owns a foundry.
If it absorbs the 2nm base die in-house, it finishes inside its own walls the step SK Hynix hands to TSMC.
If Line 2 instead starts up as planned for research and development, this report stays a report.

meru-terafab-fel-euv-light-source-vs-asm:
A signal came out of Terafab, the chip plant Musk is building in Texas, that he intends to make the light that draws the circuits himself.
Only one company in the world can make that light today, ASML of the Netherlands.

@@REF@@Musk signals interest in FEL-EUV for Terafab, potentially cutting power versus ASML's current light source (TrendForce, 2026-08-12)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/08/12/news-musk-signals-interest-in-fel-euv-for-terafab-potentially-cutting-power-vs-asmls-current-light-source/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/11135042/Terafab-SpaceX-on-X-20260811-624x293.jpg

It started with a night rendering of Terafab that began circulating on X on August 6.
A large ring runs under the building in the picture, and people asked whether that was a machine for pushing electrons to near the speed of light.
Musk answered with three letters and one more: "FEL FTW".

FEL stands for free electron laser.
It is a machine that accelerates electrons very hard and then pulls light out of them.
FTW is internet shorthand for "this is the way", so putting the two together says the light source is going to be an FEL.

## How is EUV light made

Chip circuits are drawn with light.
Drawing them finer takes light of a shorter wavelength, and what the industry uses now is extreme ultraviolet at 13.5 nanometres, EUV.

@@FLOW@@Tin droplets|fired fifty thousand times a second|High-power laser|hits each droplet and burns it into plasma|Curved mirrors|collect the light and send it to the wafer@@It burns metal to get light, which is why it drinks electricity. What Musk wants to replace is the first two steps.

An FEL has no metal to burn.
Light comes out as long as there is force pushing the electrons, and the force given back by decelerating electrons can be returned to push the next ones.
Meru writes that this is why Musk describes the route in terms of free energy.

## Changing the source changes the power bill

@@BAR@@Today's route (tin plasma)|4.4 megawatts|4.4|Free electron laser (theoretical)|0.7 megawatts|0.7@@This is the input power it takes to get one kilowatt of EUV light out. The right-hand bar is a theoretical figure, and no production lithography tool has yet shown that gap in practice.@@Cited from TrendForce reporting of 2026-08-12, accessed 2026-08-15

Electricity is the resource that runs out first for anyone building AI chips right now.
If the power behind the same light falls that far, the question of how many lithography tools fit inside one plant gets a different answer.

@@REF@@Elon Musk's Terafab enters the EUV lithography race with FEL technology (KuCoin News, 2026-08-11)|https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/elon-musk-s-terafab-enters-euv-lithography-race-with-fel-technology|https://assets.staticimg.com/@kudos/runtime/0.6.6/assets/og-ea52b6f9440e857c.jpg

That piece frames the move as a challenge to ASML's monopoly while noting in the same breath that no one has ever run production lithography off an FEL.

## Ten metres and one kilometre

Size is the price.
An ASML EUV tool is a little over ten metres long, while a machine that accelerates electrons to pull light out of them runs past a kilometre when it is built for research.
Korea has one, the fourth-generation light source accelerator run by the Pohang Accelerator Laboratory, and Meru notes that it too is more than a kilometre end to end.

Meru's reading is that the arithmetic still has a chance.
One FEL can feed light to dozens of lithography tools, and a machine built to make lithography light rather than research light can be far shorter.

## The number 2028

Musk did not raise the idea of making EUV light with an FEL first.
A US startup chaired by former Intel chief executive Pat Gelsinger is developing the same route, with the US government among its stakeholders.
What that company has promised, though, is also one prototype in 2028.
There is no FEL supplier anywhere that can feed light to volume production.

So the thing being decided now is not whether an FEL can make the light.
It already can.
What is being decided is whether that light is even and steady enough to draw circuits on a wafer, and when that gets confirmed.
If one FEL source clears production lithography inside 2028, ASML's monopoly gets a deadline attached to it for the first time; if the route is still a prototype by then, Terafab joins the queue at ASML like everyone else.

The Korean government put out two property packages together on August 13.
One is a fast-track housing supply plan meant to steady the rental and resale markets, the other a comprehensive finance package aimed at the property market.

What sits at the very top of the announcement is not a new target but an old one.
It is a line promising to improve delivery on the 1.35 million housing starts in the Seoul metropolitan area set out in the September 7, 2025 package.

The reason an existing target was restated at the top lies in that number.
Large sites such as the Yongsan International Business District, the Taereung golf course and the Gwacheon racecourse land are stalled against opposition from local governments and residents.

## When do the 230,000 arrive

The second item placed near the top is an additional 230,000 homes for the metropolitan area.
The word additional is explicit, so it is counted separately from the earlier target.

@@SHARE@@Sites already named|27,000 homes|2.7|To be announced within 2026|73,000 homes|7.3|Breaking ground after 2030|110,000 homes|11|Timing undecided|20,000 homes|2@@Almost half of the newly added volume sits beyond 2030. That report lists the breakdown of the 27,000 homes whose locations are fixed.
There are 1,000 in Yeomchang-dong in western Seoul, 21,700 around Wabu-eup in Namyangju, and 4,500 around Jangji-dong in Gwangju city, both in Gyeonggi province.

Most of the newly added volume sits outside Seoul.

## The lending side moved first

The clause that bites immediately is not one that tightens but one that loosens.
The ceiling on how much banks may grow household lending in a year was raised from 1.5% to 3.0%.
Relocation loans taken when a home is vacated for redevelopment, interim payment loans that spread the purchase price, and closing loans paid at move-in were pulled out of that ceiling altogether.

@@REF@@Korea Doubles Household Loan Growth Target to 3%, Easing Mortgage Squeeze (Seoul Economic Daily English, 2026-08-13)|https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/08/13/korea-doubles-2025-household-loan-growth-target-to-3|https://wimg.sedaily.com/news/cms/2026/08/13/news-p.v1.20260806.cf902aeb0974402e9d7df7646d865e63_P1.jpg

That report puts the effect of doubling the ceiling at roughly 30 trillion won of extra lending capacity in the second half.
The purpose of the clause is to stop bank branches from running out of mortgage quota.

On the tightening side sits the jeonse deposit loan.
Jeonse is the Korean lease in which a tenant hands the landlord a large lump sum instead of paying monthly rent, and the loan funds that sum.
A single-home owner who holds a flat in a regulated metropolitan district, does not live in it and rents it out loses access to new guarantees, and existing loans will not be rolled over at maturity.
The line between speculation and not is drawn on residence history.
It counts as speculation only if neither the owner nor the spouse has ever lived in the flat.

Read the other way, one day of registered residence by either spouse takes the household out of the rule.
The Seoul Economic Daily report notes the same carve-out, that a residency history for either spouse does not meet the speculation standard.
Because a landlord can clear the bar by moving in briefly between tenants, Meru expects the measure to do little.

## What the August 13 package leaves behind

Supply slid past 2030 while the borrowing ceiling was lifted now.
So does that combination press prices down or hold them up.

For younger buyers a door opened.
Someone aged 39 or under earning no more than 70 million won a year can borrow up to 80% of the price on a first home.
Flats in apartment complexes are excluded, so this applies only to non-apartment housing such as low-rise villas priced at 400 million won or less.

The answer turns on the starts tally early next year.
Reach the annual target and last September's package held its first year, fall short and what remains is six months in which the money available to borrow grew while the housing did not.

When supply is fixed for more than a year while demand grows, raising the price does not produce more material.

Hours before he relayed the auction result, El-Erian wrote that there is a second queue.

A purchase commitment is money already contracted to buy chips, compute, and the power and equipment that run a data centre.

Not all of that reaches the bond market.
But a commitment has to turn into cash eventually, and one route to that cash is corporate issuance.
When a government and the technology companies look for long money at the same window, the borrower is not the side that sets the price.

The thing that decides this is the November refunding.
If the Treasury lifts the share of long-dated issuance, today's yield is confirmed as a price made by supply, and if it keeps leaning on bills, the price of long money will swing more on the issuance calendar of corporations.
